newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica stocks seen up next week, rate fears abate.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica stocks seen up next week, rate fears abate.

text.p: Perceptions that a hike in South African interest rates will be delayed for the time being is seen giving shares on the Johannesburg bourse a welcome lift next week, analysts and dealers said on Friday.
Rate hike fears and a weak rand have lopped almost three percent off the market's value this month and watchers now feel the downside has been overdone.
"I don't see the negativity as being that bad that the market should continue downwards," said Rhett Hammond, a portfolio manager at Investec Asset Management.
"I see a reactive bounce, maybe a short-term slight recovery although certainly no strong running," he said.

The recovery already began to take hold on Thursday when the all-share index bounced 60.6 points or nearly one percent. On Friday, a lower bullion price gave golds shares a knock, but industrials were still surging ahead by 63.4 points to 8,043.6 by 1100 GMT. The all-share index was up 19.3 points to 6,835.5.
Economists on Thursday told Reuters an increase in the official Bank rate was unlikely immediately despite ongoing liquidity pressure in the money market.
They said Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals was likely to sit it out for now, holding the key rate at 16 percent pending further signals on money supply and the balance of payments.
Stability in the rand, which has lost around 30 percent of its value against the U.S. dollar this year, remained crucial for stocks to move up next week.
"If the rand stabilises below 4.70 we could see continued buying into this market," said James Scott, an institutional dealer at brokerage Frankel Pollak.
Without stability foreign investors who had kept a low profile in the stock market this week were not expected to return in a hurry.
"Foreigners don't want to come here because they are losing more and more on the rand every day," said Raymond Goss, a portfolio manager at Irish and Co.
The rand was last trading at 4.6700/50 against the dollar.
Local markets will have new economic data to chew over next week with the release of October consumer inflation figures on Wednesday, as well as trade balance numbers from Tuesday.
The stock market itself will have plenty to mull with some of the country's top industrial firms reporting results.

These include on Monday Barlow Ltd, Dorbyl Ltd and Adcock Ingram Ltd, and on Tuesday food group Tiger Oats Ltd. On Wednesday Tiger parent, C.G. Smith Ltd, reports annual earnings together with half year results from the Tongaat-Hulett Group Ltd.
Although firms are expected to reporting slower earnings growth than last year, stocks are seen weathering this, unless results come in well below forecasts.

"I think if we see equal to or slightly better earnings than the market average (forecast) the market should continue along its current levels or maybe slightly firmer as it is coming off quite a low base," Scott said.
